subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The SS El Faro: A Modern Ship Lost at Sea
description: A quick, practical guide to The SS El Faro: A Modern Ship Lost at Sea.

hook.text: On October 1, 2015, the cargo ship El Faro sailed into Hurricane Joaquin and sank. All 33 crew members died.

buildup.text: The captain relied on outdated weather data. The ship's route took it directly into the hurricane's strengthening path.

discovery.text: The 40-year-old ship had open scuttles near the waterline. Waves flooded the cargo hold, causing the ship to list.

twist.text: The voyage data recorder, found at 15,000 feet, revealed the captain dismissed crew concerns about the storm's severity.

climax.text: NTSB investigations led to new requirements for enclosed lifeboats and better weather routing on cargo ships.

punchline.text: Old ship. Old data. New storm. Fatal combination.

quiz.question: What key factor contributed to the sinking of the El Faro?
options: The ship struck a submerged reef that wasn't on navigation charts
The captain used outdated weather data and sailed directly into a strengthening hurricane
A fire in the engine room disabled the ship's steering and power
